note: Synthetic, obviously-fake reconciliation fixtures: one per AI-capability primitive (CP-01..CP-12), run through RuleEvaluationEngine against the full 40-rule corpus (data/rulebook.json) to see which DS rules fire and which the attack slips past. All fixtures reuse fixture field names already present in data/rulebook.json's trigger_schema trees; no new fields were invented in the fixture data itself - where a primitive has no representable field, that is recorded as `missing_fields` on the fixture rather than fabricated. Not real transactions, not real customers. Loaded via agents.loader.load_fixture_set() and scripts/reconcile_capability_primitives.py.

fixtures.label: CP-01: real-time deepfake/face-swap liveness bypass at video-KYC onboarding, followed by rapid-drain of a profile-inconsistent deposit
fixtures.representation_note: identity_markers=['edited'] maps directly onto DS-09's accepted value set (forged/deepfake_media/edited/liveness_bypass) - a photo-edit/liveness-bypass is recorded as 'edited', the closest literal value; a dedicated 'liveness_bypass' value already exists in the schema for a future, more precise fixture. DS-28 also fires here (new_account + rapid_withdrawal) - a genuine, expected overlap with DS-01, not a fixture error.

fixtures.label: CP-02: real-time voice cloning used to impersonate staff / vish a step-up or call-back authorisation
fixtures.representation_note: No field anywhere in the 40-rule corpus represents staff impersonation, vishing, or call-back/step-up authentication - this control surface (internal authentication of instructions, not customer transaction behaviour) is entirely absent from the corpus.

fixtures.label: CP-03: AI-generated synthetic identity documents used to open an account
fixtures.representation_note: identity_markers=['forged'] fires DS-09 directly (renamed from the old forged_document_provided/edited_id_photograph_provided booleans, which are not fields the rulebook's trigger_schema recognises). The PEP/sanctions-screening half this primitive is meant to stress still has no customer-side field in the corpus - DS-16's counterparty_sanctioned is scoped to counterparty wallets/transactions, not the onboarding customer, so it does not cover this half.

fixtures.label: CP-04: photo-enhanced stolen-identity reanimation supported by fake employment records
fixtures.representation_note: identity_markers=['edited'] fires DS-09 directly (renamed from the old edited_id_photograph_provided/forged_document_provided booleans, which are not fields the rulebook's trigger_schema recognises). Employment/vendor due diligence is a distinct control domain (staff/vendor onboarding, not customer AML/KYC) with no field or rule anywhere in the corpus - the fake-employment-record half still slips through entirely.

fixtures.label: CP-05: automated multi-language victim engagement (pig-butchering) drip-feeding a scam-victim through repeated transfers to a small counterparty set
missing_fields: significant_profit_or_loss (no corresponding rulebook field - profit/loss magnitude is not represented anywhere in the corpus)
fixtures.representation_note: Field names renamed to match the rulebook's actual trigger_schema fields: party_lacks_transaction_knowledge -> lacks_transaction_knowledge (DS-08); sender_unfamiliar_with_va_technology + sender_unfamiliar_with_custodial_wallet -> collapsed into the single crypto_naive field DS-12 actually checks; repeated_transactions_with_subset -> clustering (DS-15). Caught across three independent mule/scam-victim-profile rules - DS-08 (victim lacks transaction knowledge), DS-12 (victim crypto-naive), DS-15 (clustering/small counterparty set). significant_profit_or_loss has no matching field anywhere in the corpus and is recorded under missing_fields rather than left in as a fabricated field name.

fixtures.label: CP-06: AI-generated fake SMS/email impersonating a bank or exchange to redirect a payment
fixtures.representation_note: No field anywhere in the corpus represents payee-name verification or confirmation-of-payee outcomes - APP/impersonation fraud of this kind is entirely outside what the 40 rules can see.

fixtures.label: CP-07: AI-generated replica exchange app harvests credentials, attacker takes over the (existing, not new) account and drains it to an unhosted wallet
fixtures.representation_note: Value fix, not a field-name fix: unhosted_wallet was set to false, contradicting the fixture's own label ('drains it to an unhosted wallet'), which is why DS-04 never fired. Corrected to true. DS-26 (unhosted_wallet/self_custody) also fires - a genuine overlap with DS-04. NOTE: this fixture is now identical to CP-07-replica-app-unhosted-drain; if a distinct hosted-wallet account-takeover scenario (which DS-04 would genuinely miss) is wanted, this one should be redrafted with unhosted_wallet=false and expect_fired=[] instead - flagging for a decision rather than inventing that scenario unasked.

fixtures.label: CP-07 variant: harvested-credential takeover where the drain destination is an unhosted wallet
fixtures.representation_note: Companion fixture isolating the unhosted_wallet=true case so DS-04's fire is unambiguous. DS-26 (unhosted_wallet/self_custody) also fires on the same field - a genuine overlap, added to expect_fired rather than left as an unexplained extra.

fixtures.label: CP-08: synthetic-identity reuse to reopen/unfreeze a previously flagged account, using clean-looking documents and a fresh (non-shared) device/IP specifically to evade cross-account linkage
fixtures.representation_note: Deliberately modelled as evading DS-06 and DS-09: a competent synthetic-identity kit presents clean, unshared device/IP/credential fingerprints (the corpus has no field for a persistent biometric/device link back to the ORIGINAL frozen account) and documents that pass basic forgery/edit checks. Nothing in the corpus fires. This is the corpus's most direct blind spot for cross-account persistent identity linkage.

fixtures.label: CP-09: AI-assisted reconnaissance and victim targeting (upstream aggravating factor, precedes any transaction)
fixtures.representation_note: Not a transaction-level control surface by the primitive's own description ("upstream aggravating factor") - it has no fixture-representable footprint of its own. Recorded here for completeness, not counted as a corpus DRIFT GAP in the same sense as CP-02/CP-06/CP-08: no rule SHOULD be expected to fire directly on reconnaissance activity; it manifests only through the downstream primitives it aggravates (e.g. CP-05).

fixtures.label: CP-10: commoditised dark-LLM tooling (FraudGPT/WormGPT-class) used as a force multiplier across other primitives
fixtures.representation_note: Same treatment as CP-09: the primitive's own description ("force multiplier, not a control surface") means it has no transaction-level footprint of its own to fixture - it shows up only via the primitives it accelerates (e.g. CP-03, CP-06). Not counted as a corpus DRIFT GAP in the same sense as the others.

fixtures.label: CP-11: AI-orchestrated structuring - transfer amounts computed to sit just under the reporting threshold
fixtures.representation_note: DS-02's below_threshold trigger is amount-pattern-based, not actor-based, so it fires identically whether a human or an AI planner computed the sub-threshold amounts. DS-38 (sub-threshold/round amount with no stated economic rationale) also fires on the same below_threshold field with economic_rationale absent - a genuine overlap, added to expect_fired rather than left as an unexplained extra.

fixtures.label: CP-12: AI-automated mule-network / bulk account generation fanning funds in from many bulk-created accounts sharing device/IP fingerprints, then consolidating
missing_fields: ip_shared_with_other_account / device_fingerprint_shared_with_other_account (no corresponding rulebook field - only credential sharing, not IP/device fingerprint sharing, is represented)
fixtures.representation_note: credentials_shared_with_other_account renamed to shared_credentials, the field DS-06's trigger_schema actually checks - the old name was never recognised by the engine, which is why DS-06 silently failed to fire. Caught by both the fan-in/consolidation pattern (DS-05) and the shared-credentials pattern (DS-06). The IP- and device-fingerprint-sharing signals this primitive also implies have no corresponding field in the corpus and are recorded under missing_fields rather than left in as fabricated field names.

fixtures.label: Clean pass: routine, fully-compliant customer/transaction touching every field in the 40-rule corpus - none of the 40 rules should fire
fixtures.representation_note: Baseline negative control for the reconciliation run.
